# Miqsat Ma'ase Ha-Torah Section 5 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 4QMMT (4Q394–399, Cave 4), Section B concluded + beginning of C | **Condition:** Fragmentary; reconstructed from multiple manuscripts

---

**5:1** And concerning [...] the daughters of Israel and the holy seed [...] and that one should not [...] a woman who is a harlot [...]

**5:2** [...] for [...] the holy seed of the sons of Aaron [...] and also the seed of Israel [...]

**5:3** [...] One should not allow the holy seed to become intermingled with [...] nor should one permit [...]

**5:4** [...] for they are holy [...] and it is written: "You shall not bring the wages of a harlot into the house of the LORD your God" [...]

**5:5** And concerning the tithe of the grain, the wine, and the oil: the priests should be [...] the first to extend their hands to the first fruits [...]

**5:6** [...] and the Levites [...] shall receive the tithe [...] from the children of Israel [...]

**5:7** [...] And concerning the tithe of the tithe [...] the priests shall receive it from the Levites [...]

**5:8** [...] for [...] we hold that the tithe of the grain is comparable to the first fruits [...] belonging to the priests [...]

**5:9** [...] One should not withhold the tithe [...] for these are holy offerings [...]

**5:10** And concerning [...] the Ammonite, and the Moabite, and the one of illegitimate birth, and the eunuch shall not enter the assembly [...]

**5:11** [...] and they should not [...] take wives from among them [...] nor should they be admitted [...]

**5:12** [...] for [...] the assembly of the LORD is holy [...] and it is written [...]

**5:13** [...] And concerning the leper [...] the one who bears the affliction of leprosy [...] should not approach the holy purity [...]

**5:14** [...] until the sun sets on the eighth day [...] and he has been purified [...]

**5:15** You know that we have separated ourselves from the majority of the peo[ple and from all] their uncleanness,

**5:16** and from being associated with these matters, and from participating [...] in these things [...]

**5:17** [...] and you know that no [...] unfaithfulness regarding any of these matters is found among us [...]

**5:18** [...] for [...] we have separated ourselves for the sake of these matters [...]

**5:19** [...] and we have [...] withdrawn from the midst of the multitude [...] and from all their impure practices [...]

**5:20** And concerning [...] we have written to you so that you may understand the Book of Moses [and the words of the Prophets and of David...]

**5:21** [...] and the chronicles of each generation [...] and in the book it is written [...]

**5:22** [...] that [...] you would turn aside from the path [...] and that calamity would befall you [...]

**5:23** [...] and it is written: "And it shall come to pass, when all these things come upon you" [...]

**5:24** [...] "at the end of days, the blessing and the curse" [...]

**5:25** [...] "and you shall take it to heart and return to Him with all your heart and with all your soul" [...]

---

*LOGOS notes: Section B concludes with rulings on marriage purity, tithing, and assembly exclusions. LOGOS renders zonah as "harlot" (formal biblical register) rather than EMET's "prostitute." "One of illegitimate birth" renders mamzer more precisely than "bastard." The tithe-of-the-tithe ruling (5:7) reflects the sectarian insistence that priests receive their portion from the Levitical tithe, a position debated in rabbinic literature. Section C's opening (5:15) is a foundational statement of sectarian identity. "Withdrawn from the midst of the multitude" echoes Num 16:21. The scriptural citations in 5:23–25 draw on Deut 30:1–2, connecting the author's legal arguments to covenant theology. LOGOS capitalizes "Book of Moses," "Prophets," and the other scriptural divisions.*
